Haiqing Heavy Industry Machinery Co., Ltd. v. Jiangsu Zhongxing Construction Co., Ltd. and China Construction Bank Co., Ltd., Taixing Sub-branch — dispute over a construction project contract

【Ruling Summary】

In construction project activities, the basic construction procedures must be strictly followed, adhering to the principle of survey first, then design, and finally construction. If the project owner fails to deliver the geological survey report in advance, or the construction design drawings have not been reviewed and approved by the construction administrative department, the project owner shall bear primary responsibility for quality issues arising from special geological conditions that were not foreseeable by the parties at the time of contract signing. The construction contractor shall act in good faith, adopt a reasonable construction plan, and avoid the escalation of losses.

The People's Court shall, based on the construction procedures stipulated in the contract, laws, and administrative regulations, and in accordance with the principle of good faith, reasonably determine the allocation of responsibility between the project owner and the construction contractor for quality issues in the construction project.

Civil Judgment of the Supreme People's Court

(2012) Min Ti Zi No. 20

Applicant for Retrial (Plaintiff at First Instance, Counterclaim Defendant, Appellant at Second Instance): Haiqing Heavy Industry Machinery Co., Ltd., domiciled at Beigang Industrial Park, Economic Development Zone, Huludao City, Liaoning Province.

Legal Representative: Cao Keqian, General Manager of the company.

Agent ad litem: Chen Bo, lawyer of Shandong Qilu Law Firm.

Agent ad litem: Ji Jie, lawyer of Shandong Qilu Law Firm.

Respondent (Defendant at First Instance, Counterclaim Plaintiff, Appellee at Second Instance): Jiangsu Zhongxing Construction Co., Ltd., domiciled at No. 26 Jichuan Road, Taixing City, Jiangsu Province.

Legal Representative: Ni Daoren, Chairman of the company.

Agent ad litem: Li Huadong, lawyer of Jiangsu Longpan Law Firm.

Agent ad litem: Xu Xiaolong, employee of the company.

Respondent (Defendant at First Instance, Appellee at Second Instance): China Construction Bank Co., Ltd., Taixing Sub-branch, domiciled at No. 1 Tongjiang Road, Taixing City, Jiangsu Province.

Person in Charge: Ni Hongwei, President of the Sub-branch.

The applicant for retrial, Haiqing Heavy Industry Machinery Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Haiqing Company), in the case of a dispute over a construction project contract with the respondents Jiangsu Zhongxing Construction Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Zhongxing Company) and China Construction Bank Co., Ltd., Taixing Sub-branch (hereinafter referred to as Taixing Construction Bank), disagreed with the civil judgment (2010) Su Min Zhong Zi No. 0012 rendered by the Jiangsu High People's Court and applied to this Court for a retrial. This Court rendered the civil ruling (2010) Min Shen Zi No. 912-1 on November 14, 2011, ordering a retrial of this case. This Court lawfully formed a collegial panel and heard this case on April 25, 2012. The agents ad litem of Haiqing Company, Chen Bo and Ji Jie, and the agents ad litem of Zhongxing Company, Li Huadong and Xu Xiaolong, appeared in court for the proceedings. Taixing Construction Bank, having been served with a summons by this Court, failed to appear. This case is now concluded.

The Lianyungang Intermediate People's Court of Jiangsu Province (hereinafter referred to as the court of first instance) found the following facts after trial: On December 1, 2007, Haiqing Company issued an invitation for bids for the foundation works of a heavy steel structure plant. Its bidding documents stated that the quotation was only for the construction of the pile foundation and foundation of the steel structure plant (all items within the drawings); the bidder was to independently quote based on the plant foundation design drawings and requirements provided by the tenderer, as well as the bidding document requirements, according to the material market, with a fixed price covering all risks. The bidding documents also contained other content. Zhongxing Company's bid price was RMB 15.1065 million, and its budget price was RMB 13.6898 million. The earthwork excavation plan submitted by Zhongxing Company in its bid specified excavation requirements, internal and external dewatering of the foundation pit, traffic organization for foundation pit excavation, excavation methods, precautions for foundation pit excavation, potential problems that may arise during excavation and corresponding corrective measures, and safety production measures. Among the precautions for foundation pit excavation, item (1) stated that the excavation depth should be strictly in accordance with the foundation structure construction drawings; item (5) stated that if the soil quality at the bottom of the pit was found to be inconsistent with the survey report after excavation, the owner, supervisor, and design institute should be promptly notified.

On December 15 of the same year, Zhongxing Company won the bid. On the same day, the parties signed the "Steel Structure Plant Pile Foundation and Foundation Engineering Contract" (hereinafter referred to as the "Contract"), agreeing as follows: The construction period for the pile foundation and foundation works of Haiqing Company's heavy steel structure plant was 60 days (from December 20, 2007, to the date when the project met acceptance conditions by February 22, 2008, and Haiqing Company was notified in writing of the date of completion for acceptance); the project scope: the pile foundation and foundation works of the heavy steel structure plant (all works within the drawings), with the drawings attached as an appendix to the contract; the contracting method was fixed-price labor and materials (including all costs such as materials, labor, machinery, material inspection and reporting fees); the project cost was RMB 13.3 million, which was the total amount for the completed and accepted project and was a fixed price. Changes in the quantity of works due to design changes were to be negotiated separately by the parties by way of a supplementary agreement. Within three working days after the contract took effect, Haiqing Company was to pay Zhongxing Company 20% of the total project cost, i.e., RMB 2.66 million; the required project quality was qualified; Haiqing Company's rights and obligations were: during Zhongxing Company's construction, Haiqing Company had the right to supervise quality and progress on site. It was to establish a quality inspection team responsible for supervising and accepting the project construction, composed of members from the supervision company and Haiqing Company's technical personnel. The quality inspection team was to conduct random inspections of project progress and quality. For issues such as quality problems in material processing, unqualified construction, or failure to meet schedule requirements, it had the right to stop the construction. Haiqing Company's representative could raise opinions, and Zhongxing Company was to adopt corresponding corrective measures to ensure quality. Haiqing Company was to provide three connections and one leveling for Zhongxing Company, provide benchmarks and coordinate points, conduct on-site handover, and organize joint review of drawings by relevant units. Zhongxing Company's rights and obligations were: to strictly construct according to the drawing design requirements and relevant national specifications and standards, to ensure quality and quantity, and to guarantee the project is completed on time; to formulate detailed and reliable construction plans and safety assurance measures, etc. The parties agreed that after signing the contract, neither party could unilaterally terminate the contract; otherwise, the breaching party would pay the non-breaching party a lump-sum liquidated damages of RMB 1 million; if Zhongxing Company had major quality issues or failed to meet the technical standards and requirements stipulated in this contract, for each day it delayed Haiqing Company's normal commencement or normal production, Zhongxing Company would pay Haiqing Company liquidated damages equal to 3 per thousand of the total contract price, and so on, and bear all economic losses caused to Haiqing Company. Haiqing Company and Zhongxing Company were jointly responsible for handling all pre-commencement inspection procedures, pile foundation testing, and external coordination work. Regarding contract changes, modifications, and termination: if (1) Zhongxing Company became bankrupt or incapable of construction; or (2) Zhongxing Company breached and failed to perform other obligations stipulated in the contract, Haiqing Company could notify Zhongxing Company in writing, proposing to terminate the contract in whole or in part. Zhongxing Company should immediately refund all payments made by Haiqing Company. The appendices to the contract were the bidding documents, the bid invitation document, the letter of acceptance, and the fax correspondence between the parties. The contract also stipulated payment of project funds, warranty period, acceptance, and other matters.

The pile location layout diagram provided by Haiqing Company stated: The foundation design of this project is based on the "Detailed Geotechnical Engineering Survey Report" (November 2007) for Phase I of Haiqing Company prepared by Lianyungang Civil Design Institute Co., Ltd. The foundation design grade was Class B, and the safety grade for building piles was Level 2. During foundation pit excavation, attention should be paid to protecting the pile body, and temporary soil stockpiling is strictly prohibited next to the piles. Pile foundation construction should strictly comply with the "Technical Code for Building Pile Foundations," etc.

On December 16 of the same year, Haiqing Company provided the geotechnical survey report and a general site plan to Zhongxing Company, one copy each.

On December 20 of the same year, Zhongxing Company commenced construction on site. On December 26, Zhongxing Company sent two work contact sheets to Haiqing Company, the main content of which was that due to the complex geological conditions on site, the original natural soil was the silt soaked in water, etc., the current earthwork quantity greatly exceeded the contract's scope of works, and dewatering was required. It was suggested to raise the indoor ±0.00 elevation and the site elevation to reasonable positions, request the design institute to increase pile lengths to raise the pile caps (and modify the pile caps), and solve the drainage problem.

On December 27 of the same year, Taixing Construction Bank issued a "Performance Bond" to Haiqing Company, the main content of which was: it assumed joint and several liability for Zhongxing Company's performance of the obligations stipulated in the Contract, the maximum guarantee amount not exceeding RMB 2.6 million, with the guarantee period from December 27, 2007, to February 26, 2008. The bond also guaranteed other terms. On February 22, 2008, Taixing Construction Bank extended the expiry date to March 30, 2008.

On December 30, 2007, Zhongxing Company sent a work contact sheet to Haiqing Company, the main content of which was that due to road problems, transport vehicles could not deliver materials to the site, requesting an acceleration of road repair.

On February 19, 2008, Haiqing Company and Zhongxing Company signed a "Supplementary Agreement" stipulating that the construction period was extended to March 30, 2008, with a penalty of RMB 10,000 for each day of delay. The contract also stipulated other terms.

On February 26, Zhongxing Company sent a report to Haiqing Company, stating that the current earthwork quantity greatly exceeded the contract works scope, and it was all silt, requesting Haiqing Company to take measures, otherwise it would apply for an extension of the construction period. On February 27, Zhongxing Company sent a report to Haiqing Company, stating that due to the unqualified construction site roads, the earthwork for secondary handling collapsed, making normal construction impossible.

On February 27, Haiqing Company replied to Zhongxing Company regarding the reports of the 26th and 27th, the main content being: The construction contract signed by both parties stipulated a fixed total price for a completed and accepted project, an unchangeable price (except for design changes). Regardless of whether the geological conditions were silt or clay, we consider that the contractor conducted a site survey of the construction location before signing the contract and understood the on-site geological conditions. Therefore, all matters related to construction should be handled by the contractor and are unrelated to Haiqing Company.

On February 28, Zhongxing Company sent a letter to Haiqing Company, the main content being: 1. Our unit was only provided with the geological survey report by your company after we pointed out, following the signing of the contract, that piles could not be driven. 2. Our unit did conduct a site inspection before signing the contract, but your company had already backfilled the site before the inspection and did not inform our unit. During excavation, large areas of silt were discovered. 3. The total earthwork excavation and backfill quantity in our unit's bid was only 10,000 cubic meters; now, before the A-axis excavation was even completed, the excavated earthwork had already exceeded the total earthwork quantity in the entire bid. 4. Our unit submitted multiple construction plans for approval, but your company did not approve any of them. 5. The excavation test conducted by your company caused the excavated pile caps to collapse again due to silt. If no feasible excavation measures are provided in reply to our unit, our unit will stop all construction on March 2, 2008, and your company shall compensate for losses and bear additional liability for breach of contract.

On March 11, Haiqing Company notified Zhongxing Company of a change in the quantity of works. On the same day, Zhongxing Company notified the supervision unit of the occurrence of Class III and IV piles and proposed treatment measures for Class III and IV piles. The supervision unit, after consultation with Haiqing Company, agreed to the treatment measures for Class III piles and stated that the related costs would be borne by Zhongxing Company. For Class IV piles, treatment opinions approved by the design unit were required.

On March 15, Haiqing Company, Zhongxing Company, and the supervision unit reached a meeting minutes, the main content being: For the A-axis, except for Class IV piles, the work required to reach the design elevation of -1.5 meters was to be completed by the morning of the 19th; for the B-axis, after the treatment of Class III and IV piles was completed, all works were to be completed within 10 days. The contractor was to strictly follow construction. If the above tasks were not completed on time, the contractor would automatically withdraw from the site.

On March 19, Zhongxing Company submitted a written report to Haiqing Company and the supervision unit, stating that the current Class III and IV piles had made it impossible to proceed normally with the subsequent construction procedures, and requesting a joint analysis and discussion of the causes for the Class III and IV piles in the afternoon. In the afternoon of the same day, a meeting was held by Haiqing Company, Zhongxing Company, the supervision unit, the testing unit, and the design unit, and minutes were formed. The main content was that the cause of the Class III and IV pile problem was related to the geological conditions and heavy machinery rolling, requiring ground treatment.

On March 25, Zhongxing Company submitted a written report to Haiqing Company and the supervision unit, stating that due to soil quality issues, subsequent construction procedures could not be carried out.

On March 26, the supervision unit sent a work contact sheet to Zhongxing Company, stating that the A-axis work was to be suspended, and construction could only resume after the design institute issued a treatment plan; other cleaning work was to continue.

On March 28, Zhongxing Company submitted a foundation pit support plan and detailed drawings to Haiqing Company and the supervision unit. The next day, a meeting minutes on the support plan was reached by Zhongxing Company, Haiqing Company, and the supervision unit, the main content being that Haiqing Company's drawings had been submitted for review and approved, and Zhongxing Company proposed the support plan for submission for review.

On March 31, experts from Zhongxing Company, Haiqing Company, the supervision unit, Lianyungang City Construction Bureau, Lianyungang City Construction Project Quality Supervision Station, Lianyungang City Construction Project Drawings Review Center, and Lianyungang Yujian Construction Engineering Appraisal Co., Ltd., among other units, jointly discussed the foundation pit support research plan. At the meeting, Haiqing Company required Zhongxing Company to produce calculation sheets for the support plan for confirmation. The experts confirmed that both of Zhongxing Company's plans were feasible, mainly depending on cost and construction period. On the same day, Lianyungang Yujian Construction Engineering Appraisal Co., Ltd. issued the "Demonstration Opinion on the Foundation Pit Enclosure Design Plan for Haiqing Company's Coal Chemical Equipment Manufacturing Plant Foundation," which was submitted to Haiqing Company on April 5. The "Demonstration Opinion" considered that both "Design Plans" from Zhongxing Company were feasible, with Haiqing Company selecting the preferred option. Lianyungang Yujian Construction Engineering Appraisal Co., Ltd. also provided opinions for deepening and improving the design plans.

On April 1, Zhongxing Company submitted a foundation pit protection cost statement to Haiqing Company. On April 2, Zhongxing Company sent a letter requesting Haiqing Company to select and confirm the foundation pit support plan.

On April 6, Zhongxing Company sent a letter to Haiqing Company, the main content being that because Haiqing Company did not provide the geological survey report during the bidding, Zhongxing Company's quotation and the compiled bidding plan were based on normal construction procedures. Foundation pit support was not within the original construction scope, and the schedule delay was due to the lack of on-site conditions, etc.

On April 30, Zhongxing Company reported to Haiqing Company, requesting that solutions be provided as soon as possible to resume construction.

On May 21, commissioned by Haiqing Company, and specified and selected for inspection by Haiqing Company and the supervision company, pile foundation quality testing was conducted. The total number of piles constructed between February 16 and March 10, 2008, was 1,476, of which 474 were tested. Jiangsu Jianxiang Engineering Testing Co., Ltd. issued Testing Report No. 2008-X-X17-3 on the pile foundation quality of Haiqing Company's coal chemical plant (partial). The report concluded: A total of 474 piles were tested by low-strain method, including 90 Class I piles; 83 Class II piles; 210 Class III piles (referring to piles with obvious defects affecting the structural bearing capacity of the pile body); 91 Class IV piles (referring to piles with severe defects). Neither party disputed the conclusion of this testing report.

On May 24, Haiqing Company sent a letter to Zhongxing Company, requesting termination of the contract and requiring Zhongxing Company to assume liability for breach of contract and compensate for economic losses of RMB 5.75 million. On May 26, Zhongxing Company replied, requesting continued performance of the contract.

On May 30, Haiqing Company filed a lawsuit with the court of first instance, alleging that it had invested a total of RMB 7.72 million in the project execution, but due to Zhongxing Company's reasons, the project quality had serious problems. After several rounds of negotiations, Zhongxing Company prevaricated using various excuses and failed to take timely corrective measures, causing the subsequent works to be unable to proceed normally, ultimately preventing Haiqing Company from commencing production on schedule. At the time, due to Zhongxing Company's breach of contract, the contract signed by both parties could not be performed normally. Terminating the contract was necessary to avoid further escalation of losses. Therefore, Haiqing Company requested: 1. A ruling confirming the validity of the notice of termination and terminating the contract; 2. An order that Zhongxing Company assume liability for breach of contract and compensate for economic losses of RMB 5.72 million; 3. An order that Taixing Construction Bank assume joint and several liability and fulfill its guarantee obligation; 4. The litigation costs be borne by Zhongxing Company and Taixing Construction Bank.

Zhongxing Company filed a counterclaim, alleging that Zhongxing Company had invested RMB 13,335,172 in the project, and Haiqing Company still owed RMB 5,615,172. Additionally, because Haiqing Company lacked the sincerity to continue performing the contract, it caused Zhongxing Company to be idle and have work stoppages for a long period, with losses already reaching RMB 1,978,846, for which Haiqing Company should compensate. Furthermore, due to the special foundation conditions, the design and construction plans had to be changed, and the project cost could not be resolved by the amount stipulated in the original contract. The cost for the foundation pit support alone would exceed RMB 10 million. Haiqing Company had not acknowledged this, and the contract could not be performed. Zhongxing Company requested a ruling terminating the "Contract" signed by both parties, and ordering Haiqing Company to pay the project cost and losses totaling RMB 7,594,018, with all litigation costs in this case borne by Haiqing Company.

The court of first instance also found that during the construction of the disputed project, Haiqing Company conducted batch quality acceptance inspection on procedures such as Zhongxing Company's axis positioning, foundation pile positions, earthwork excavation, reinforcement engineering (raw materials, reinforcement processing), concealed works, concrete engineering (raw materials, mix design), and formwork engineering, all of which were accepted as qualified. Haiqing Company confirmed during the court trial that Zhongxing Company constructed the pile lengths and pile caps according to the drawings. Haiqing Company paid a total of RMB 7.72 million in project funds to Zhongxing Company from January 2 to March 13, 2008.

It was further found that Haiqing Company stated during the trial of the court of first instance that the disputed project had not yet obtained a construction project permit or construction work permit. The project drawings had been reviewed, but because the fees were not paid, Haiqing Company had not yet obtained the reviewed drawings.

During the proceedings at first instance, upon the application of Zhongxing Company, the court of first instance commissioned relevant institutions to conduct appraisals and evaluations on the project quality and project cost, respectively. Regarding the project cost, Lianyungang Yong'an Cost Consulting Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Yong'an Cost Consulting Company) issued Report No. 2009-108, the "Cost Appraisal Report for the Foundation Works of Haiqing Company's Heavy Steel Structure Factory Building," with the following conclusions: the completed works for the foundation works amounted to RMB 11,338,644.49; losses during the suspension period amounted to RMB 2,518,309.41, of which labor costs were RMB 880,750, material costs were RMB 1,581,058.77 (including RMB 1,289,133.17 for materials used in the physical works, comprising RMB 1,179,873.9 for steel bars, RMB 71,630 for anchor bolts, and RMB 37,629.27 for steel bar fabrication; and RMB 291,925.60 for temporary works materials, comprising RMB 9,935 for carbon steel plates, RMB 104,676 for scaffolding couplers, RMB 7,560 for seamless steel tubes, RMB 55,200 for wooden formwork, RMB 77,059.6 for scaffolding steel pipe rental, and RMB 331,568.64 for scaffolding steel pipe purchase; the above materials were sealed up during the trial of the first instance court upon the application of Haiqing Company), and machinery costs were RMB 56,500.64. The report explained: the quantity of completed works was calculated based on on-site measured quantities combined with the construction drawings; material prices were generally based on the Lianyungang guiding prices for December 2007, but there were no guiding prices for piles, so the unit price for piles was derived from the unit price of piles in the case files after deducting piling costs, and the unit price for pile tips was based on the unit price stated in the relevant documents in the case files. Due to significant price fluctuations for steel bars during the construction period, the unit price for steel bars was set at RMB 4,700 per ton based on documents from relevant government authorities, the Lianyungang guiding prices for February 2008, and the case file materials. The material losses for the suspension period were calculated as the acquisition costs for raw physical materials; the costs for semi-finished physical materials included acquisition costs and processing costs; the temporary works materials mainly consisted of scaffolding steel pipes and couplers, and rental costs and acquisition costs were calculated based on the leasing contracts in the case files.

Lianyungang Construction Project Quality Supervision Station issued Report No. Lian Zhi Jian (2009) 001, the "Project Quality Appraisal Report," regarding the tilting and cracking of the disputed project works, with the following appraisal analysis opinions: (I) The tilting and cracking of the project piles in this work were caused by the following factors during construction: 1. On-site observation: Because the earth transportation route was only subject to simple backfill and compaction, without special reinforcement treatment, the soil outside the foundation pit was subjected to rolling and compaction by heavy vehicles, causing settlement, creep, and sliding, which increased the soil pressure on the foundation pit, and this was one of the main factors causing the tilting, deformation, and cracking of the project piles. 2. According to the geological report, the evaluation of the foundation soil at the site was: the foundation pile caps of this project were located on the marine silt layer, and the slope ratio for the foundation pit excavation should have been approximately 1:7 based on calculations, i.e., to protect the project piles in the foundation pit from damage, the safe slope distance for the excavation slope of the foundation pit should have been 21 meters, and without retaining walls and roadbed reinforcement measures, heavy trucks and excavating machinery with a load greater than 4 tons per square meter could not operate within approximately 18 meters from the edge of the foundation pit. However, for this project, precisely the above-mentioned errors were committed. 3. Before the commencement of this project, the construction unit and the supervision unit did not go through the procedures for examination of construction drawings, quality supervision, and safety supervision in accordance with the normal construction procedures for capital construction, which prevented the project from being carried out under a proper construction regime. The supervision unit failed to exercise oversight; before the civil construction unit commenced excavation of the foundation pit earth, the supervision unit did not review the earth excavation plan prepared by the construction unit in accordance with the spirit of Ministry of Construction Document No. 213 (2004) and Lianyungang City Documents Lian Jian (2005) No. 175 and Lian Jian (2006) No. 577. At the same time, it failed to take effective measures to stop the civil construction unit from excavating the earth before the earth excavation plan had been reviewed, and to stop the construction unit from interfering with the excavation and transportation of earth within the foundation pit. Therefore, it also bears some responsibility for this quality incident of tilting and cracking of the pile foundations. If the construction unit had submitted the design and construction drawings for review before the start of this project, and if the construction unit had followed normal construction procedures before the excavation of the foundation pit earth, and had prepared a detailed construction plan in accordance with the above-mentioned documents from the Ministry of Construction and Lianyungang City, submitted it to the supervisor for review, organized expert demonstration, and then carried out the construction, then this quality incident of pile tilting and cracking could have been avoided. (II) The appraisal unit conducted a technical site visit to the construction site. According to the construction unit's account: 1. Before the pile foundation construction on December 26, 2007, the construction unit suggested extending the pile length, keeping the ±0.00 unchanged and raising the pile caps upward to reduce the depth of foundation pit excavation, but the construction unit did not receive a reply. 2. Before the pile foundation construction and the foundation pit earth excavation, the construction unit did not provide the geological investigation report, and the provided construction drawings had not been reviewed by the Lianyungang City Construction Project Drawing Review Center as required. 3. The construction unit participated in the excavation and transportation of earth in the foundation pit, interfering with the normal construction of the construction unit. 4. Based on this, the analysis considered that if the above-reported circumstances were true, they would have a significant impact on the quality of the pile foundation construction. If the construction and supervision units had submitted the construction drawings for review as suggested, and had reported to the design unit the need to extend the pile length and raise the pile cap elevation, and had followed capital construction procedures, then this quality incident could have been mitigated or avoided.

In the first instance, Haiqing Company raised objections to the standardization of this appraisal conclusion, arguing that it had not participated in the on-site inspection and had not confirmed the authenticity of the inspection materials, and therefore did not recognize the appraisal report. In light of Haiqing Company's refusal to recognize the appraisal report and its failure to raise specific substantive objections, the court of first instance clarified during the trial that if Haiqing Company wished to provide a face-to-face or written response, it should submit specific written objections. Haiqing Company replied that it would submit written objections after the trial but failed to do so. Zhongxing Company expressed recognition of the appraisal conclusion.

The court of first instance held that the focus of the dispute between the parties was: 1. who was responsible for the quality issues arising in this project; 2. whether Zhongxing Company had committed a breach of contract in the performance of the contract; 3. the amount of the project funds in this case.

The court of first instance held that the contract concluded between the parties through the bidding process represented the true intent of the parties, and its content did not violate the prohibitive provisions of national laws and regulations, and thus was a valid contract. With regard to the contract signed by the parties, since both parties agreed to rescind the contract during the proceedings, the court of first instance so ordered.

Regarding the issue of whether Zhongxing Company had committed a breach of contract in the performance of the contract. In this case, as the bidding party, Zhongxing Company prepared the bid documents and project budget based on the bidding documents and factory building foundation design drawings provided by the bidding party Haiqing Company. In the bid documents, Zhongxing Company also explicitly stated in the main matters concerning foundation pit excavation that "the construction shall be strictly in accordance with the foundation structure construction drawings; if after excavation of the foundation pit, it is found that the soil quality at the bottom of the pit does not conform to the survey report, the owner, supervisor, and design unit shall be promptly notified." Based on the work contact sheets of Zhongxing Company, it can be confirmed that Zhongxing Company fulfilled its reporting obligation. Based on the acceptance records of batch quality acceptance, which were all deemed qualified by Haiqing Company and the supervision unit, it can be proven that Haiqing Company conducted on-site supervision of quality during Zhongxing Company's construction process. With regard to the construction of pile length and pile caps, Haiqing Company also confirmed at trial that Zhongxing Company had constructed strictly in accordance with the drawings. Combined with the analysis opinions in the project quality appraisal conclusion, it can be confirmed that Zhongxing Company did not violate the contract during the performance of the contract. Haiqing Company's claim that Zhongxing Company breached the contract lacked factual basis, and the court of first instance did not support its request for Zhongxing Company to bear liability for breach of contract. At the same time, Taixing Construction Bank did not violate the commitments made under the "Contract Guarantee," and Haiqing Company's request for Taixing Construction Bank to assume liability under the guarantee lacked factual and legal basis, and this request was also not supported by the court of first instance.

Regarding the issue of responsibility for the quality of the pile foundation works in question. Article 11 of the Regulations on Quality Management of Construction Projects provides that the construction unit shall submit the construction drawing design documents to the administrative department of construction of the people's government at or above the county level or other departments for review. Construction drawing design documents that have not been reviewed and approved shall not be used. In this case, although Haiqing Company submitted the relevant construction drawings to Zhongxing Company and acknowledged during the proceedings that Zhongxing Company had constructed in accordance with those drawings, the drawings submitted by Haiqing Company were not reviewed construction drawings. At the same time, Zhongxing Company had already reported the geological conditions to Haiqing Company in a work contact sheet dated December 26, 2007, and requested that Haiqing Company consult the design institute to increase the pile length and raise the pile caps. This reporting act by Zhongxing Company complied with the requirements of the earth excavation plan in its bid documents, and Haiqing Company should have responded promptly. Under the circumstances where the construction drawings were not reviewed and Haiqing Company did not respond to Zhongxing Company's report of abnormal geological conditions, the consequences arising therefrom should be borne by Haiqing Company itself. In addition, according to the minutes of meetings during the construction process, it can be confirmed that Haiqing Company interfered with Zhongxing Company's normal construction during the excavation of the foundation pit. Combined with the fact that during the quality appraisal process, the parties jointly selected Lianyungang Construction Project Quality Supervision Station as the quality appraisal unit, and that station conducted a site inspection at Haiqing Company's construction site during the appraisal process, in the absence of sufficient contrary evidence and reasons that Haiqing Company could provide to rebut the appraisal, the court of first instance recognized the appraisal conclusion of the "Project Quality Appraisal Report" of Lianyungang Construction Project Quality Supervision Station. Haiqing Company's claim that it was not notified of the on-site inspection and that the authenticity of the inspection materials was not confirmed was not accepted by the court of first instance. With regard to the relevant procedures of the project in question, Haiqing Company conducted batch quality acceptance, and the acceptance results were all qualified, which further proves this point. In summary, based on the appraisal conclusion and the specific acts of the parties in performing the contract, the court of first instance held that Haiqing Company should bear responsibility for the quality issues that arose during the construction of the pile foundations.

Regarding the amount of the project funds. The conclusion of the cost appraisal report from Yong'an Cost Consulting Company was: the completed works for the foundation works amounted to RMB 11,338,644.49; losses during the suspension period amounted to RMB 2,518,309.41, of which labor costs were RMB 880,750, material costs were RMB 1,581,058.77 (RMB 1,289,133.17 for materials used in the physical works and RMB 291,925.60 for temporary works materials), and machinery costs were RMB 56,500.64. As for this cost appraisal conclusion, Haiqing Company expressed its non-acceptance but did not raise specific substantive objections. The court of first instance did not support this. As for the quantity and price of steel bars, the appraisal unit calculated the quantity of steel bars based on the drawings and adjusted the price by reference to the market price. Zhongxing Company argued that the quantity of steel bars it actually used was more than 100 tons greater than that in the appraisal conclusion and that the price should be based on the market price in March 2008. In the absence of evidence from Zhongxing Company to prove the actual quantity of steel bars used in the project, the court of first instance did not accept this objection. As for the unit price of earthwork, when there was a significant discrepancy between the actual earthwork volume and the budgeted volume in the case, it was not improper for the appraisal unit to calculate on an actual basis. Zhongxing Company's request to calculate the total price based on the budget unit price lacked factual basis and was not supported.

In summary, the price of the works completed by Zhongxing Company was RMB 11,338,644.49, the labor cost loss during the suspension period was RMB 880,750, the material cost was RMB 1,581,058.77, and the machinery cost loss was RMB 56,500.64, totaling RMB 13,856,953.90. Haiqing Company had paid RMB 7,720,000 in project funds, leaving a balance of RMB 6,136,953.90, which Haiqing Company should pay to Zhongxing Company, plus interest on the bank loan for the same period from the date Zhongxing Company filed its counterclaim.

On September 9, 2009, the court of first instance rendered Civil Judgment (2008) Lian Min Yi Chu Zi No. 0067: 1. The "Contract" signed between Haiqing Company and Zhongxing Company on December 15, 2007, was rescinded; 2. Haiqing Company's other claims were dismissed; 3. Haiqing Company shall pay to Zhongxing Company project funds in the amount of RMB 6,136,953.90 plus interest (interest shall be calculated at the People's Bank of China loan rate for the same period, from June 25, 2008, to the date of payment as determined by the judgment) within ten days after the judgment takes effect; 4. Zhongxing Company's other claims were dismissed. The court filing fee for the main action was RMB 48,690, to be borne by Haiqing Company. The court filing fee for the counterclaim was RMB 32,480, of which Zhongxing Company was to bear RMB 1,480 and Haiqing Company was to bear RMB 31,000. The preservation fee of RMB 5,000 was to be borne by Haiqing Company. The project cost appraisal fee of RMB 110,000 was to be borne by Zhongxing Company in the amount of RMB 10,000 and by Haiqing Company in the amount of RMB 100,000. The project quality appraisal fee of RMB 29,900 was to be borne by Haiqing Company.

Haiqing Company, dissatisfied with the judgment of first instance, appealed to the Jiangsu Higher People's Court (hereinafter referred to as the court of second instance), arguing: 1. The findings of fact in the judgment of first instance were erroneous. (1) Regarding the issue of time limits. The time limit originally stipulated in the contract signed by Haiqing Company and Zhongxing Company was from December 20, 2007, to February 22, 2008. Later, due to various reasons raised by Zhongxing Company, the parties, after negotiation, reached a "Supplemental Agreement" on February 19, 2008, extending the time limit to March 30, 2008. On March 6, 2008, the parties again agreed in a "Supplemental Agreement" that the time limit would still expire on March 30, 2008. Thereafter, the parties did not reach any further agreement on the time limit. Although Zhongxing Company later negotiated with Haiqing Company regarding the foundation pit support plan and costs, the foundation pit support plan was within the scope of work agreed upon in Zhongxing Company's contract, and the costs were already included in the lump-sum contract price. Therefore, the subsequent negotiations could not serve as a reason for Zhongxing Company to extend the time limit. Consequently, the delay from March 31, 2008, onward should be the responsibility of Zhongxing Company, and Zhongxing Company should bear liability for breach of contract. (2) Regarding the issue of the "Detailed Geotechnical Investigation Report" and the design drawings. First, the design drawings were based on the "Detailed Geotechnical Investigation Report," and the design drawings had been reviewed and confirmed to have no substantive issues; construction in accordance with the design drawings could fully meet the project quality requirements. Second, Zhongxing Company had reviewed the "Detailed Geotechnical Investigation Report" during the bidding process, and the design drawings were the basis for its preparation of the bid documents. Third, Zhongxing Company received the "Detailed Geotechnical Investigation Report" and the design drawings on the day after the parties signed the contract and before the actual start of construction, giving it ample time to formulate a reasonable and scientific construction plan. Finally, the (2009) No. 001 "Project Quality Appraisal Report" did not determine that the absence of the "Detailed Geotechnical Investigation Report" was the cause of the substandard construction quality. Based on materials accepted by both parties, it was sufficient to prove that the "Detailed Geotechnical Investigation Report" and the design drawings were not the cause of the delay, because when the parties re-agreed on the completion date in the "Supplemental Agreement," they had fully considered various factors and Zhongxing Company's requests. (3) Regarding other acts of breach of contract by Zhongxing Company in the performance of the contract. The "Project Quality Appraisal Report" clearly stated: (a) the earth transportation route was only subject to simple backfill and compaction, which was one of the main factors causing the tilting, deformation, and cracking of the project piles; (b) the slope ratio was incorrect; (c) the construction unit did not follow normal construction procedures, etc. These issues were the consequences of Zhongxing Company's failure to construct in accordance with specifications, which constituted a material breach of contract, and Zhongxing Company should bear liability for breach of contract as stipulated in the contract. (4) Certain parts of the "Project Quality Appraisal Report" were erroneous. First, Haiqing Company did not adopt Zhongxing Company's suggestion because the suggestion was only for Zhongxing Company's convenience in construction but did not comply with the design requirements of the design unit or Haiqing Company's future use requirements. Second, the claim that the construction unit interfered with the normal construction of the construction unit was purely fictitious. Third, the appraisal report itself stated that it was based on information provided by the construction unit, which had not been verified through court proceedings. Although the "Project Quality Appraisal Report" mentioned the fault of the construction unit, it did not point out that Zhongxing Company's failure to construct in accordance with national specifications and its failure to construct in accordance with the commitments made in the bid documents were the primary causes of the quality issues in this case. In this case, Zhongxing Company neither provided foundation pit support nor piled soil alongside the piles for a long time, resulting in serious quality issues. The judgment of first instance made erroneous findings on all the above issues. 2. The proceedings in the first instance were improper. During the first instance, the appraiser for the "Project Quality Appraisal Report" did not appear in court to be questioned, and Haiqing Company also did not accept the "Cost Appraisal Report." First, with regard to the cost of the completed works, the parties had explicitly agreed on a lump-sum fixed price of RMB 13,300,000. Without considering quality issues, Zhongxing Company had completed less than half of the work, yet the appraisal cost was RMB 11,338,644.49, which clearly did not conform to the parties' agreement. Haiqing Company believed that, regardless of quality issues, the entire project cost should be appraised, and then the completed cost should be determined by the formula: RMB 11,338,644.49 / total project cost × RMB 13,300,000. Second, the suspension losses were entirely appraised based on materials submitted solely by Zhongxing Company that had not been verified through evidence. 3. The application of law in the first instance was erroneous. Most of the works completed by Zhongxing Company were substandard, and although the appraisal conclusion was erroneous, it was sufficient to prove that Zhongxing Company bore significant fault for the substandard quality; and the suspension of the project was entirely caused by Zhongxing Company's reasons, so the suspension losses should be borne by Zhongxing Company itself. The judgment of first instance ordering Haiqing Company to pay Zhongxing Company the project funds and bear the suspension losses constituted an erroneous application of law. In summary, [Haiqing Company] requested a change of the judgment according to law, support for Haiqing Company's claims, and dismissal of Zhongxing Company's counterclaims.

Zhongxing Company made an oral defense: 1. Regarding the issue of construction period. The reasons for the delay in the construction period in this case: (1) The geological conditions at the construction site were severely inadequate, the ground was entirely silt, and the moisture content was too high, causing the pile driving to be unable to be fixed, which inevitably led to cracks. Haiqing Company bears responsibility for this issue, as it provided the geological survey report after the signing of the construction contract, resulting in the contractor submitting a bid and quote without knowledge of the geological conditions, which was far lower than the actual cost. After receiving the geological survey report, Zhongxing Company had already proposed corresponding remedial measures, but Haiqing Company did not adopt them. (2) Haiqing Company failed to fulfill its contractual obligation to provide "three connections and one leveling," resulting in the inability to carry out normal construction. (3) Changes and increases in the relevant quantity of work affected the construction period. (4) After discovering the poor geological conditions, Zhongxing Company repeatedly requested Haiqing Company to modify the design and even proactively drafted plans, but Haiqing Company did not respond. (5) After problems arose with the pile foundation, Zhongxing Company actively contacted the expert group and Haiqing Company to find the cause, draft feasible plans, and submit a budget, but Haiqing Company never responded. (6) Haiqing Company's grounds of appeal contradict the agreement reached during the performance of the contract. During the performance of the contract, Haiqing Company acknowledged the extension of the construction period, agreed that the A-axis construction should proceed only after the design institute's plan was issued, and the B-axis construction should be completed within 10 days after the handling of the third and fourth type pile issues. Given that the parties had reached this agreement, Zhongxing Company neither had the fact of delaying the construction period nor should it bear liability for the delay. 2. Regarding the issue of project quality. (1) The quality appraisal report has already clearly determined that the project quality problems were not caused by Zhongxing Company's construction; (2) The acceptance records for each individual quality item at every step of the project were all satisfactory and complied with construction specifications; Zhongxing Company constructed in accordance with the drawings; (3) Zhongxing Company did not completely and mechanically construct according to the drawings; after discovering the geological problems, it had already proposed solutions to Haiqing Company, but these were not adopted; (4) Due to the poor geological conditions of the construction site, the project quality was inherently deficient; (5) Zhongxing Company's proposed plan to raise the pile cap was not adopted; if this opinion had been adopted, the quality problems could have been avoided; (6) Haiqing Company interfered with the contractor's construction; (7) The construction drawings were not submitted for review as required, which would inevitably lead to quality problems; (8) The lump-sum price in the construction contract was based on ordinary geological conditions. After Zhongxing Company received the geological survey report and discovered the special geological conditions, this should constitute a change in the project. 3. Regarding the project cost and loss amounts, the conclusion of the first instance appraisal is correct. 4. Regarding procedural issues. (1) At the first instance trial, Haiqing Company's objections to the quality appraisal report were too general. The court required it to list the issues in detail, and Haiqing Company stated on the spot that it would submit written materials after the trial, but has not submitted them to date. This should be deemed a waiver of its rights, and the first instance procedure was not improper; (2) Although Haiqing Company raised objections to the appraisal of the project cost, these were insufficient to overturn the appraisal conclusion. 5. Regarding the application of law, this is left to the court's judgment. In summary, the request is to dismiss Haiqing Company's appeal and affirm the first instance judgment.

Taixing Construction Bank did not make a defense.

The court of second instance found that both parties had no objection to the facts ascertained by the first instance court and confirmed them.

During the second instance trial, Haiqing Company submitted the "Construction Drawing Design Review Opinion Letter" issued by Lianyungang City Construction Drawing Review Center on April 15, 2008, and the "Opinion Feedback Form" issued by Zhejiang University of Technology Institute of Architectural Design and Planning on November 15, 2009, to prove that the construction drawings issued by the design unit had already been reviewed by the relevant authorities. Zhongxing Company, during cross-examination, argued that the "Construction Drawing Design Review Opinion Letter" and the "Opinion Feedback Form" were made only after the project quality accident occurred and could no longer prevent the accident. Moreover, the opinion letter had already pointed out problems in the design and required modifications and adjustments in consultation with the survey and design units, indicating that the construction drawing review had not passed.

The court of second instance considered that the issues in dispute in this case were: 1. The cause and responsibility for the quality problems in the disputed project; 2. Whether Zhongxing Company should bear liability for breach of contract; 3. How the project payment and losses due to work stoppage should be determined.

(I) Regarding the cause and responsibility for the quality problems in the disputed project.

The court of second instance held that, according to the "Project Quality Appraisal Report" issued by Lianyungang City Construction Project Quality Supervision Station, the accident involving the tilt and fracture of the piles in the project in question was caused by a combination of several factors. Upon specific analysis of these factors, it should be determined that both the construction unit and the construction company should bear corresponding responsibilities.

1. Haiqing Company, before the construction of the project, failed to go through the procedures for construction drawing review, quality supervision, and safety supervision in accordance with the normal construction procedures for capital construction, creating hidden dangers for the occurrence of the quality accident. Haiqing Company should bear responsibility for this. Haiqing Company submitted the "Construction Drawing Design Review Opinion Letter" issued by Lianyungang City Construction Drawing Review Center during the second instance trial. In this opinion, the evaluation of the safety and rationality of the foundation treatment and structural design stated "No violation of mandatory provisions or mandatory standards," but also noted that "Because the pile cap is buried deep in flowing plastic silt, the design should remind the contractor to do a good job of foundation pit support, and the equipment foundation should be constructed simultaneously." The comprehensive review opinion stated: "1. The depth and completeness of the construction drawing design documents are basically in compliance with regulations. 2. Each discipline has content that does not meet the design specifications and standards, and modifications and improvements should be organized according to the review opinions. 3. Adjustments and modifications to the original design should be made in the form of corrective measures and formal design changes, and after re-inspection, if qualified, approval shall be granted." The court of second instance held that, from the content of the "Construction Drawing Design Review Opinion Letter," it had already discovered the potential hazards posed by the special soil quality of the construction site and the pile cap height in the design plan and had raised corresponding requirements. If the construction unit, supervision unit, and design unit had received this opinion letter in a timely manner and given it due attention, taking corresponding protective measures or adjusting the design plan, the occurrence of the quality accident might have been mitigated or avoided. However, because the date of issuance of this opinion letter was April 15, 2008, by which time the project quality accident had already occurred, the issuance of the opinion letter was clearly too late to be of any help. Therefore, it should be determined that there is a causal relationship between Haiqing Company's failure to submit the construction drawings for review as required by the "Regulations on Quality Management of Construction Projects" and other regulations before construction and the occurrence of the project quality accident, and Haiqing Company should bear corresponding responsibility.

2. Due to the relatively special geological conditions of the area where the project in question is located, the foundation pile caps rest on a marine silt layer. The slope coefficient for foundation pit excavation, calculated based on these conditions, should be approximately 1:7, meaning that to protect the engineering piles in the foundation pit from damage, the safe slope distance for the foundation pit excavation slope should be 21 meters. However, the actual slope width of the project was far less than 21 meters, which is one of the main reasons for the project quality accident. Regarding the responsibility for insufficient slope width, the court of second instance held that both the construction unit and the construction company bear certain responsibilities. First, the earthwork excavation plan prepared by Zhongxing Company stated "The soil slope gradient shall not exceed the safe gradient (1:1.5)," which clearly could not meet the safety requirements of the foundation pit. In response, Zhongxing Company argued that it received the geotechnical survey report from the construction unit only one day after signing the contract, resulting in its bid quote, made without knowledge of the geological conditions, being far lower than the actual project cost required. It repeatedly requested Haiqing Company to increase the project funds, but Haiqing Company ignored these requests, preventing it from adjusting the construction plan and increasing the earthwork excavation volume. The court of second instance held that, considering the timing of when Zhongxing Company received the geotechnical survey report from the construction unit (after the signing of the contract), it was objectively difficult for Zhongxing Company to make an accurate judgment of the local special geological conditions at the time of signing the contract. It could only base its bid and prepare the earthwork excavation plan on general geological conditions. However, after receiving the geotechnical survey report before construction, Zhongxing Company already had knowledge of the site conditions and could make a correct judgment. At that point, Zhongxing Company should have been aware that the original earthwork excavation plan might create quality hazards and had the obligation to promptly report to the owner, supervision unit, and design unit to readjust the earthwork excavation plan. Of course, if the slope were widened according to the 1:7 requirement in the appraisal conclusion, it would result in a substantial increase in project cost, potentially causing a fundamental change in the basis of the contract. In this situation, both parties should have acted in good faith, renegotiated, and jointly agreed on a feasible excavation plan and contract price. However, Zhongxing Company only proposed an optimized design plan for increasing pile length and raising the pile cap. After this plan was not adopted by the construction unit, it failed to further request the construction unit to adjust the excavation plan out of concern for project quality and safety, instead proceeding with the original plan. Therefore, Zhongxing Company should bear a certain responsibility for the quality consequences arising from the construction. Haiqing Company insisted that the project cost was a fixed price and, on the grounds that the construction method adopted by the contractor during construction was unrelated to the construction unit, failed to give due attention or respond to the contractor's suggestions for adjusting the design plan, and should also bear a certain responsibility. Additionally, before the contractor started earthwork excavation within the foundation pit, the supervision unit failed to effectively review the earthwork excavation plan prepared by the contractor in accordance with the spirit of documents from the Ministry of Construction and the Lianyungang Municipal Construction Authorities, and failed to take effective measures to stop the contractor's excavation activities that might affect project quality and the phenomenon of the construction unit interfering with the earthwork excavation and transportation within the foundation pit. Therefore, the supervision unit should also bear a certain responsibility for the quality accident caused by insufficient slope width during foundation pit excavation. Since this case deals with the dispute between the construction unit and the contractor, and the supervision unit acts as the agent of the construction unit to supervise and manage project quality, the responsibility of the supervision unit in this case should also be considered as the responsibility of the construction unit. In summary, regarding the issue of insufficient slope coefficient, the construction unit, Haiqing Company, should bear primary responsibility, and the contractor, Zhongxing Company, bears secondary responsibility.

3. In this project, the earth transportation route was only simply backfilled and compacted without special reinforcement treatment. Without enclosure and roadbed reinforcement measures, trucks and excavation machinery with a load greater than 4 tons per square meter could not travel within a range of 6H (approximately 18 meters) from the edge of the foundation pit. However, in this project, the settlement, creep, and sliding of the soil outside the foundation pit caused by the rolling of heavy vehicles increased the soil pressure inside the foundation pit and was one of the main factors causing the tilting, deformation, and fracture of the engineering piles.

Regarding the rolling compaction by heavy vehicles and excavation machinery, according to Zhongxing Company's work contact sheet dated February 28, 2008, it can be proven that Haiqing Company, during the construction, organized its own excavators and large earth-moving vehicles to carry out foundation pit excavation. This work contact sheet was signed off by the supervision unit. Although Haiqing Company denied this, it did not provide sufficient evidence to overturn it, so the court of second instance confirmed this evidence. Haiqing Company argued that the excavation machinery and earth-moving vehicles used by Zhongxing Company also contributed to the soil subsidence. The court of second instance held that although Zhongxing Company also used excavation machinery, its impact on soil subsidence was far less than that of large earth-moving vehicles. As for whether Zhongxing Company used trucks for earth moving, Haiqing Company failed to provide evidence proving that Zhongxing Company's earth moving work did not meet construction specifications, so the court of second instance did not support its claim.

Regarding the responsibility for not reinforcing the earth transportation route, the court of second instance held that the "Contract" only stipulated that the construction unit should provide the contractor with "three connections and one leveling" conditions, but did not specifically stipulate whether this included roads within the construction site. Where the contract terms were unclear, according to Article 61 of the Contract Law of the People's Republic of China, the parties should supplement the terms by agreement; if a supplementary agreement could not be reached, it should be determined according to the relevant terms of the contract or trade practices. In this case, although Zhongxing Company issued a work contact sheet to the construction unit requesting road repair, Haiqing Company did not respond, which cannot be deemed as the parties having reached an agreement on supplementing the original contract. According to industry practice for construction engineering contracts, roads used for construction are temporary roads for the project. Unless explicitly stipulated otherwise in the contract, they should be borne by the contractor. Therefore, in this case, the responsibility for not reinforcing the construction road should be borne by Zhongxing Company, while the primary responsibility for the rolling compaction by heavy vehicles and excavation machinery should be borne by Haiqing Company.

In summary, the court of second instance held that, before the construction of the pile foundation project in question, Haiqing Company failed to submit the construction drawings for review in accordance with relevant state regulations before handing them over to the contractor for construction, leaving hidden dangers for project quality. After the special geological conditions causing difficulties in the construction were discovered during the construction process, neither party actively acted in good faith. As the construction unit, Haiqing Company failed to work with the supervision unit and the design unit to give due attention to the contractor's reasonable suggestion of "increasing pile length and raising the pile cap" and to study corresponding measures, and also failed to work with the supervision unit to review the contractor's earthwork excavation plan and conduct expert论证. As the contractor, Zhongxing Company failed to reasonably adjust the earthwork excavation plan according to the special soil quality requirements and submit it to the supervision unit for review, instead mechanically proceeding with construction according to the construction drawings and the original excavation plan. Additionally, during construction, Zhongxing Company did not reinforce the roads, and Haiqing Company used heavy trucks to participate in earthwork excavation and transportation, interfering with normal construction. Both parties were at fault. After comprehensively analyzing and comparing the above factors, the court of second instance held that the construction unit should bear 80% of the responsibility for the occurrence of the project quality problems in this case, and the contractor should bear 20% of the responsibility.

(II) Regarding whether Zhongxing Company should bear liability for breach of contract.

Haiqing Company argued that, according to the contract between the parties, if Zhongxing Company had a major quality problem or failed to meet the technical standards and requirements stipulated in the contract, for each day it affected Haiqing Company's normal commencement or normal production, Zhongxing Company should pay Haiqing Company liquidated damages equal to 3‰ of the total project cost as stipulated in the contract.

The court of second instance held that the fundamental cause of the quality problems in the project in question was the relatively special geological conditions of the area where the project was located. Neither party fully anticipated these geological conditions when signing the contract. After discovering during the performance of the contract that the soil quality affected the construction, the parties should have, in good faith, negotiated the adjustment of the construction plan and contract price, fairly and reasonably determined their respective rights and obligations, and performed the contract. However, because both parties failed to fulfill their obligations in accordance with the principle of good faith, it resulted in a delay in the construction period and a project quality accident, leading to huge losses in construction costs. For the occurrence of these losses, based on the degree of fault of each party, Haiqing Company should bear primary responsibility, and Zhongxing Company should bear secondary responsibility.

In addition to the loss of construction costs, Haiqing Company also claimed that Zhongxing Company should bear liability for breach of contract due to the delay in the construction period, which prevented the project from being completed and put into use on time. In response, the court of second instance held that since the primary fault for the failure to complete the project on time due to the quality problems lies with Haiqing Company, Haiqing Company's claim for Zhongxing Company to bear liability for breach of contract regarding the construction period, beyond the construction costs, lacks a sufficient legal basis and is not supported.

(III) Regarding how the project payment and losses due to work stoppage should be determined.

The project cost conclusion made by Yongan Cost Consulting Company was: cost for completed works of the foundation project: RMB 11,338,644.49; losses during the work stoppage period: RMB 2,518,309.41, including: labor costs: RMB 880,750, material costs: RMB 1,581,058.77 (materials for the engineering entity: RMB 1,289,133.17, measure materials: RMB 291,925.60), machinery costs: RMB 56,500.64. Total: RMB 13,856,953.90. Haiqing Company raised the following objections to the cost appraisal conclusion:

1. Objection to the method of appraising the project cost. Haiqing Company argued that the contract between the parties specified a fixed price, and the appraised cost should also be according to the contract, i.e., the appraised cost of completed works divided by the cost of construction according to the drawings, multiplied by the fixed price stipulated in the contract.

2. The list of materials recognized in the appraisal report as losses of Zhongxing Company was provided unilaterally by Zhongxing Company and cannot be used as a basis for determining the facts.

3. The contract between the parties was already terminated on May 24, 2008, and the machinery was not left on the construction site, so calculating the machinery work stoppage loss up to November 30, 2008, is inconsistent with the facts.

4. Zhongxing Company only had two or three management personnel and twenty or thirty workers. The cost appraisal adopted the labor wages based on materials unilaterally provided by Zhongxing Company without cross-examination, lacking a basis.

The court of second instance held that: 1. Regarding the appraisal method. In response to the objection raised by Haiqing Company, the appraiser replied during the second instance trial that, although the contract between the parties stipulated a fixed price, because the project was not yet completed and the cost of measure expenses incurred during the construction was relatively large, it was difficult to accurately calculate the proportion of the completed work volume to the total work volume solely by appraising the cost based on the construction drawings. Therefore, the court of second instance held that the method proposed by Haiqing Company for calculating the cost by dividing the appraised cost of completed works by the total project cost and multiplying by the fixed price of RMB 13.3 million was not reasonable. The appraisal institution's calculation of the completed works based on actual quantities was not improper and should be upheld.

2. Regarding the losses of materials such as rebar, steel tubes, and fasteners, as well as machinery losses, these were all losses caused by the litigation preservation applied by Haiqing Company during the first instance. Although the amounts were calculated based on the list provided by Zhongxing Company, they were already inventoried by the first instance court during the litigation preservation period. Haiqing Company did not raise any objections during the process of the first instance court taking preservation measures. Therefore, its claim on appeal lacks evidentiary support and is not upheld.

3. Regarding labor wage losses. In this case, the appraisal institution calculated the labor losses based on the payroll provided by Zhongxing Company. The management personnel wages were calculated from April to November 2008, totaling RMB 168,000; worker wages were calculated from April to June 2008, until the parties agreed to terminate the contract during the first instance litigation, totaling RMB 712,750; additionally, worker severance costs of RMB 50,000 were calculated, totaling RMB 880,750. Although Haiqing Company raised objections, it could not provide sufficient counter-evidence to overturn this; moreover, from the perspective of time and amount, the calculation is not unreasonable, so it should be upheld.

In summary, the court of second instance held that the cost of completed works and losses during the work stoppage period for Zhongxing Company amounted to RMB 13,856,953.90. For this loss, Haiqing Company should bear 80% of the responsibility, and the remaining 20% should be borne by Zhongxing Company itself. Therefore, Haiqing Company should pay Zhongxing Company RMB 11,085,563.12. Currently, Haiqing Company has already paid RMB 7.72 million in project payments, leaving an outstanding balance of RMB 3,365,563.12. Haiqing Company should pay this amount to Zhongxing Company and bear the corresponding bank loan interest for the same period for Zhongxing Company.

The court of second instance rendered Civil Judgment (2010) Su Min Zhong Zi No. 0012 on March 2, 2010, holding as follows: 1. Affirm item 1 of the judgment of first instance, namely, rescind the Contract entered into between Haiqing Company and Zhongxing Company on December 15, 2007; 2. Affirm item 2 of the judgment of first instance, namely, dismiss the other claims of Haiqing Company; 3. Affirm item 4 of the judgment of first instance, namely, dismiss the other counterclaims of Zhongxing Company; 4. Amend item 3 of the judgment of first instance as follows: Haiqing Company shall pay Zhongxing Company project payment of RMB 3,365,563.12 and interest thereon (interest calculated at the loan interest rate for the same period published by the People's Bank of China, from June 25, 2008 to the date of payment) within ten days after this judgment becomes effective.

Court acceptance fee for the action at first instance was RMB 48,690, to be borne by Haiqing Company. Court acceptance fee for the counterclaim was RMB 32,480, of which Zhongxing Company shall bear RMB 6,496 and Haiqing Company shall bear RMB 25,984. Preservation fee of RMB 5,000 shall be borne by Haiqing Company. Project cost appraisal fee of RMB 110,000, of which Zhongxing Company shall bear RMB 22,000 and Haiqing Company shall bear RMB 88,000. Project quality inspection fee of RMB 29,900, of which Zhongxing Company shall bear RMB 5,980 and Haiqing Company shall bear RMB 23,920. Court acceptance fee for the second instance was RMB 32,480, of which Haiqing Company shall bear RMB 25,984 and Zhongxing Company shall bear RMB 6,496.

Haiqing Company, dissatisfied with the civil judgment (2010) Su Min Zhong Zi No. 0012 of the High People's Court of Jiangsu Province, filed an application for retrial with this Court, requesting: to set aside the civil judgment (2010) Su Min Zhong Zi No. 0012 of the High People's Court of Jiangsu Province and render a new judgment in accordance with law. At the retrial hearing, Haiqing Company clarified its claims in retrial as follows: to order Zhongxing Company to bear liquidated damages of RMB 5.72 million; to order Taixing Construction Bank to assume joint and several liability within the scope of the guarantee letter; to dismiss Zhongxing Company's counterclaim; and to have all litigation costs borne by Zhongxing Company. Thereafter, upon clarification by this Court, Haiqing Company abandoned its claims against Taixing Construction Bank in the retrial.

The facts and reasons on which Haiqing Company applied for retrial are as follows:

(A) The original judgment found the facts incorrectly. 1. There was no causal relationship between the fact that the design drawings had not been reviewed in advance and the project quality problems. 2. The proposal put forward by Zhongxing Company to "increase pile length and raise the pile cap" was only for the convenience of the construction personnel, but did not meet the design requirements of the design unit or the needs of Haiqing Company; moreover, "increasing pile length and raising the pile cap" would affect the load-bearing capacity, thereby affecting the foundation safety of the factory building, and construction could only proceed after the design unit had recalculated and re-designed the drawings. The original design drawings had no problems, and the Design Drawing Review Opinion did not put forward any substantive opinions either. 3. There was no evidence confirming that the road was damaged by Haiqing Company. Haiqing Company and the supervision unit had never received the work contact sheet from Zhongxing Company dated February 28, 2008; even if they had received it, it would only prove that Haiqing Company had conducted an excavation test for about one day, and there was no record of large earth-moving vehicles transporting soil. In this case, the construction unit was Zhongxing Company, and it was correct to find that it had used machinery and vehicles to complete the vast majority of the excavation and all of the earth-moving work. With respect to liability for the damage to the piles caused by the road damage, Zhongxing Company should bear at least 99% of the liability. 4. The second instance found that the slope coefficient for the excavation in this project was insufficient, and that Haiqing Company should bear the primary liability. However, since both sides of the construction road required excavation of foundation pits, if the slope coefficient was satisfied, it would be impossible to meet the requirements for construction passage. What Zhongxing Company should bear is the liability for failing to adopt a reasonable construction plan, including a shoring plan, under circumstances where the normal slope coefficient could not be satisfied, thereby leading to the quality incident. 5. It can be seen from the appraisal report that if the construction passage had been reinforced, there would have been no problem; if there had been no large or heavy vehicles passing, there would have been no problem; if foundation pit shoring had been used, there would have been no problem. However, Zhongxing Company neither reinforced the road, nor adopted a safe method for excavating the foundation pit and transporting soil, and in actual construction, it also did not adopt foundation pit shoring measures. This was the primary cause of the project quality problems in this case. The time when Zhongxing Company proposed the shoring plan was March 28, 2008, but on March 25, 2008, the pile testing results commissioned by Haiqing Company from Lianyungang Jianxiang Pile Testing Co., Ltd. showed that most of the piles were waste piles, and adopting a foundation pit shoring plan at that point was too late to remedy the situation. Moreover, assuming Zhongxing Company only learned of the geological conditions on December 16, 2007, Zhongxing Company could have chosen not to proceed; since it chose to proceed, it should have determined a reasonable and scientific construction plan, or simply suspended work to avoid greater losses, rather than only thinking about adjusting the construction plan after a serious quality problem had occurred. The allocation of liability in the second instance should be reversed, with Zhongxing Company bearing 80% of the liability. 6. Regarding the project cost appraisal report. First, the method for appraising the cost of the completed works was problematic. Not only should the cost of the completed works be appraised, but the cost of the entire project according to the drawings should also be appraised; then, the ratio of the two costs multiplied by the contract price would be the cost of the completed works by Zhongxing Company calculated in accordance with the contract. Second, regarding the calculation of wages for workers and management personnel, the appraiser simply relied on the wage list unilaterally provided by Zhongxing Company, without any other supporting evidence.
