During the trial of the second instance, Haiqing Company strongly requested that Zhongxing Company provide photocopies of the identity cards of all persons on the list and relevant certificates for the payment of pension insurance and personal income tax, but the second instance ignored Haiqing Company's legitimate doubts. The second instance's finding of the time and amount of wages was very unreasonable. During the retrial review, Haiqing Company submitted a work contact sheet from the supervision unit, which new evidence was sufficient to show that all of Zhongxing Company's construction personnel had left the site before the end of April 2008. 7. The material losses mentioned in the Project Cost Appraisal Report were not losses and should not be included as part of the project cost. The items seized by Haiqing Company upon application included steel bars, steel plates, construction scaffolding, and some equipment, etc. These materials were not incorporated into the project. After the case was concluded, Zhongxing Company could take them away, and they should not be included as part of the project cost. Moreover, on July 26, 2010, during the enforcement proceedings by the Lianyungang Intermediate People's Court, it had already been determined that the materials at the site belonged to Zhongxing Company, and Zhongxing Company had taken all the above materials away.

(B) Zhongxing Company should bear liability for breach of contract. The original contract between Haiqing Company and Zhongxing Company stipulated that the construction period was from December 20, 2007 to February 22, 2008. Later, due to various reasons raised by Zhongxing Company, the parties reached a Supplementary Agreement on February 19, 2008, extending the construction period to March 30, 2008. On March 6, 2008, the parties again agreed in another Supplementary Agreement that the construction period would still expire on March 30, 2008. Thereafter, the parties did not reach any new consensus on the construction period. Although Zhongxing Company later negotiated with Haiqing Company regarding the foundation pit shoring plan and costs, the foundation pit shoring plan was within the scope of work stipulated in Zhongxing Company's contract, and the costs were already included in the lump-sum contract price. Therefore, the later negotiations could not serve as a reason for Zhongxing Company to extend the construction period. Consequently, the delay in the construction period arising from March 31, 2008 onward should be the responsibility of Zhongxing Company, and Zhongxing Company should bear liability for breach of contract.

This Court confirms the facts found by the courts of first and second instance.

This Court is of the opinion that the issues in dispute in this case are: 1. How should liability be allocated for the quality problems that arose in the project; 2. Whether Zhongxing Company should bear liability for the delay in the construction period; 3. How to determine the project payment and the loss due to work stoppage.

1. How should liability be allocated for the quality problems that arose in the project.

Haiqing Company claimed in its application for retrial that the original judgment found the facts incorrectly and that it was wrong for it to bear the primary liability for the project quality problems. The following is a discussion of each sub-issue:

(1) Whether there is a causal relationship between the fact that the design drawings had not been reviewed in advance and the project quality problems. Haiqing Company argued that there was no causal relationship between the lack of prior review of the design drawings and the quality problems, and that the second instance was wrong to find that the review opinion concluded that the design drawings were problematic. Zhongxing Company responded that Haiqing Company failed to truthfully provide the geotechnical investigation report, and that the construction drawings had not been approved, had not been jointly reviewed, and lacked scientific论证, leading to a deviation from the local geological reality, with no specific measures designed for the soft clay layer, which caused the quality problems. Moreover, to this day, the drawings provided by Haiqing Company have still not been reviewed and do not bear the review seal.

This Court holds: Article 5 of the Regulation on Quality Management of Construction Projects provides that in carrying out construction project activities, the basic construction procedures must be strictly followed, adhering to the principle of conducting investigation first, then design, then construction. Article 11 provides that the construction entity shall submit the construction drawing design documents to the construction administrative department of the people's government at or above the county level or other relevant departments for review. Construction drawing design documents that have not been reviewed and approved shall not be used. In this case, the project quality problems arose to a large extent due to the special local geology. According to the requirements of the Regulation on Quality Management of Construction Projects, among the prescribed procedures for basic construction, the three stages most closely related to the formation of project quality are investigation, design, and construction. The investigation work provides geological, hydrological, and other conditions for the design, and gives the bearing capacity of the foundation. The investigation results document is the basic data for the design work. Based on this, the design unit determines the type of structure to be used, carries out the foundation design, and provides the construction drawings to the construction unit, which then builds according to the drawings. In this case, during the bidding process, Haiqing Company failed to provide evidence that it had provided a detailed geotechnical investigation report; instead, it only submitted it the day after the contract was signed, creating a hidden danger for the occurrence of the quality incident. Haiqing Company should bear responsibility for this.

Although Haiqing Company submitted the Construction Drawing Design Review Opinion issued by the Lianyungang Construction Drawing Review Center during the trial of the second instance, which evaluated the safety and rationality of the foundation treatment and structural design as "no violation of mandatory provisions or mandatory standards," it also stated that "because the pile cap is buried relatively deep in the soft-flowing clay, the design should remind the construction unit to properly carry out foundation pit shoring, and the equipment foundation should be constructed simultaneously." The comprehensive review opinion stated: "All specialties have content that does not meet the design codes and standards, and modifications and improvements should be organized according to the review opinions." It can be seen that the Construction Drawing Design Review Opinion had already identified the special soil conditions at the construction site and the potential hazards caused by the height of the pile cap in the design plan, and proposed corresponding requirements for "adjustment and modification of the original design should issue corrective measures and formal design changes in accordance with the format; after re-inspection and approval, it shall be passed." In this case, if the construction entity, the supervision unit, and the design unit had received this opinion in time and given it sufficient attention, taking corresponding protective measures or adjusting the design plan, the occurrence of the quality incident might have been mitigated or avoided. However, the opinion was issued on April 15, 2008, by which time the project quality incident had already occurred, so the issuance of the opinion came too late to remedy the situation. Therefore, in this case, Haiqing Company violated administrative regulations by failing to submit the construction drawings for review, and the subsequently issued Construction Drawing Design Review Opinion warned of risks and required rectification and changes. It should be found that there was a causal relationship between Haiqing Company's failure to submit the drawings for review and the occurrence of the project quality incident in this case, and Haiqing Company should bear the primary liability. Zhongxing Company, as the construction unit, also had some fault in ignoring the basic construction procedures and being eager to bid for and undertake the project despite the fact that the construction entity had not submitted the detailed geotechnical investigation report and the reviewed construction drawings. The second instance's finding of this liability was not improper. Haiqing Company's argument that there was no causal relationship between the lack of review of the design drawings and the quality problems lacked sufficient basis, and its reasons were untenable. This Court does not support this argument.

(2) Regarding the proposal by Zhongxing Company to "increase pile length and raise the pile cap." Haiqing Company claimed in its retrial that Zhongxing Company's proposal was only for the convenience of the construction personnel, but did not meet the design requirements of the design unit or the needs of Haiqing Company; moreover, "increasing pile length and raising the pile cap" would affect the load-bearing capacity, thereby affecting the foundation safety of the factory building, and construction could only proceed after the design unit had recalculated and re-designed the drawings. The original design drawings had no problems, and the Design Drawing Review Opinion did not put forward any substantive opinions either. Therefore, Haiqing Company should not bear corresponding liability for quality problems arising from this. Zhongxing Company responded that the proposal had been reviewed by experts, as could also be confirmed by the quality appraisal report, and that if the proposal had been adopted, the quality problems could have been avoided, and the cost of the proposal was relatively low.

This Court holds: After obtaining the detailed geotechnical investigation report and the general site plan on December 16, 2007, Zhongxing Company commenced construction on the site on December 20, 2007. On December 26, Zhongxing Company sent two work contact sheets to Haiqing Company, the main content of which was that due to the complex geological conditions at the site, the original natural soil was soft clay soaked in water, and the earthwork volume was far exceeding the scope of the contract quantity, and dewatering was required. It recommended raising the indoor ±0.00 elevation and the site elevation to reasonable positions, and requesting the design institute to increase the pile length and raise the pile cap (and modify the pile cap), and to address the drainage issue. In addition, in the main items for foundation pit excavation in its bid documents, Zhongxing Company also stated: "Carry out strictly in accordance with the foundation structure construction drawings; if after excavation of the foundation pit it is found that the soil quality at the bottom of the pit does not match the investigation report, promptly report to the owner, supervision unit, and design unit." It can be seen that Zhongxing Company had timely fulfilled its reporting obligation and made recommendations. Moreover, the "increasing pile length, raising pile cap" proposal was also addressed in the Project Quality Appraisal Report of Lianyungang Construction Engineering Quality Supervision Station, in the section "Appraisal and Analysis Opinion on the Inclination and Fracture of Some Project Piles of Haiqing Company's Coal Chemical Equipment Manufacturing Plant," which stated that the proposal had a significant impact on the quality issues of the pile foundation construction. If the construction entity and the supervision unit had submitted the construction drawings for review and reported to the design unit to increase the pile length and the pile cap elevation, and had followed the basic construction procedures, then the quality incident in this case could have been mitigated or avoided. However, Haiqing Company failed to work with the supervision unit and the design unit to give sufficient attention to the proposal made by Zhongxing Company and to study corresponding measures. Therefore, Haiqing Company should bear the primary liability for the subsequent project quality incident. The second instance's allocation of liability in this regard was not improper.

(3) Regarding the liability for the compaction by heavy vehicles and excavating machinery. Haiqing Company claimed in its retrial that there was no evidence confirming that the road was damaged by Haiqing Company, and that Haiqing Company and the supervision unit had never received the work contact sheet from Zhongxing Company dated February 28, 2008. Even if they had received it, it would only prove that Haiqing Company had conducted an excavation test for about one day, and there was no record of large earth-moving vehicles transporting soil. In this case, the construction unit was Zhongxing Company, and it was correct to find that it had used machinery and vehicles to complete the vast majority of the excavation and all of the earth-moving work. With respect to liability for the damage to the piles caused by the road damage, Zhongxing Company should bear at least 99% of the liability. Zhongxing Company responded that the road compaction was entirely caused by Haiqing Company. Haiqing Company itself organized large machinery for on-site excavation and large vehicles for hauling earth, which led to the road being damaged and the piles becoming inclined.

This Court holds: The work contact sheet dated February 28, 2008 stated: "On February 24, 2008, the construction entity organized its own excavators and large earth-moving vehicles to excavate the foundation pit at the intersection of axes A and 33-35, adopting a method of excavating and hauling simultaneously, resulting in soil subsidence along the roads traversed by the large earth-moving vehicles." Although Haiqing Company claimed that it had never received the work contact sheet dated February 28, 2008, the work contact sheet bore the signature of the supervision unit. The project supervision unit is a unit entrusted by the construction entity to supervise and manage the construction project within the scope of the entrustment, in accordance with national legal requirements and the requirements of the construction entity. Therefore, although Haiqing Company denied the work contact sheet, it did not provide sufficient evidence to rebut it, so it should be accepted. Moreover, Haiqing Company did not submit any evidence showing that it had ever raised an objection to the consequences of soil subsidence mentioned in the work contact sheet, which was caused by the compaction of excavators and large earth-moving vehicles organized by Haiqing Company itself. In summary, the second instance's finding of liability regarding the soil subsidence, pile inclination, and fracture caused by the compaction of Haiqing Company's heavy vehicles and excavating machinery was not improper. Haiqing Company's reason for retrial on this point lacks sufficient basis and is not supported.

(4) Regarding the issue of insufficient slope coefficient for the excavation. Haiqing Company claimed in its retrial that because both sides of the construction road required excavation of foundation pits, if the slope coefficient of 1:7 was satisfied, it would be impossible to meet the requirements for construction passage. What Zhongxing Company should bear is the liability for failing to adopt a reasonable construction plan, including a shoring plan, under circumstances where the normal slope coefficient could not be satisfied, thereby leading to the quality incident. Zhongxing Company responded that the slope coefficient met the requirements.

This Court holds: The earthwork excavation plan prepared by Zhongxing Company stated: "The slope of the earth slope shall not exceed the safe slope (1:1.5)." This excavation plan was made based on general geological conditions, but given the special geology of the project in question, it could not meet the safety requirements of the foundation pit. Although Haiqing Company did not raise any objection, after receiving the geotechnical investigation report provided by the construction entity, Zhongxing Company had become aware of the on-site geological conditions. At that point, Zhongxing Company should have noticed that the original earthwork excavation plan might cause quality hazards and had an obligation to promptly report to the owner, supervision unit, and design unit, and to adjust the earthwork excavation plan. The construction entity and the construction unit should also have acted in good faith, renegotiated, and jointly agreed on a feasible excavation plan and contract price. However, in this case, Zhongxing Company only proposed an optimized design plan of increasing the pile length and raising the pile cap. After that plan was not adopted by the construction entity, Zhongxing Company failed to further request the construction entity to adjust the excavation plan, acting in the interest of project quality and safety, and instead proceeded with the original plan. Therefore, Zhongxing Company should bear some liability for the quality consequences arising from the construction. Haiqing Company, by insisting that the project price was fixed and by taking the position that the construction method adopted by the construction unit was none of the construction entity's concern, failed to give attention or response to the construction unit's suggestion to adjust the design plan, and should also bear some liability.

(5) Regarding the foundation pit shoring issue. Haiqing Company claimed in its retrial that Zhongxing Company had clearly specified foundation pit shoring structures in its bid documents, but in actual construction, it did not adopt any shoring measures for the foundation pit, which was the main cause of the project quality incident in this case. Zhongxing Company responded that the commitment to foundation pit shoring in its bid documents was not based on any information, since at the time of bidding and signing the contract, it had not seen the geotechnical investigation report and could not have considered the issue of foundation pit shoring.

Opinion of the Court

According to the Regulations on Quality Management of Construction Projects, any person engaged in construction project activities must strictly follow the capital construction procedures, adhering to the principle of survey first, design second, and construction last. The geological conditions of the area where the project in question was located were relatively special. Considering the time when Zhongxing Company received the geotechnical investigation report provided by the project owner, it was after the parties signed the contract. Therefore, it was objectively difficult for Zhongxing Company to make an accurate judgment on the local special geological conditions at the time of bidding and even when signing the contract. Although Zhongxing Company's bid documents stated that "if local displacement of the support structure is found to be large and exceeds the permissible range during excavation, excavation should be temporarily suspended, and diagonal bracing should be applied in the vertical plane using steel pipes or steel cable ties, while unloading outside the support structure to reduce active earth pressure; anchoring bolts may also be driven for reinforcement; if cracks appear in the support structure, bracing reinforcement may be applied between the support structure and the support piles using steel pipes or steel cable ties," this support scheme should be considered as made for general geology rather than the special geology of the project in question. Zhongxing Company formulated a foundation pit support scheme on March 28, 2008, and sought expert review. The result was an increase in project cost of over RMB 10 million, which is corroborated by the fact that the contract budget price for this project was approximately RMB 13 million. After discovering the special geological conditions, both the constructor and the project owner should act in good faith, negotiate, and adjust the plan. In this case, Zhongxing Company proposed a relevant plan, while Haiqing Company insisted that the project cost was a fixed lump sum and took a negative attitude, stating that the foundation pit support scheme and costs proposed by Zhongxing Company had nothing to do with the project owner. Haiqing Company should bear primary responsibility for the quality problems that arose. Although Zhongxing Company proposed the foundation pit support scheme on March 28, 2008, on May 21, 2008, Haiqing Company commissioned a testing entity to conduct random tests on the pile foundation during the pile construction period (February 16, 2008, to March 10, 2008). Major quality problems had already occurred in the pile foundation. The occurrence of these quality problems is somewhat related to the fact that, after signing the contract and discovering the special geology, Zhongxing Company made suggestions but then proceeded with construction recklessly despite Haiqing Company's non-acceptance. Therefore, Zhongxing Company should also bear a certain degree of responsibility.

In conclusion, both the project owner and the constructor were at fault for the major quality problems in the project in question. Haiqing Company violated the principle of good faith by failing to submit the detailed geotechnical engineering investigation report and the reviewed construction drawings before signing the contract, thereby violating the basic construction procedures stipulated in the Regulations on Quality Management of Construction Projects and laying the groundwork for the quality accident. Haiqing Company failed to work with the supervision unit and the design unit to give adequate attention to and study corresponding measures for the constructor's reasonable proposal to "increase pile length and raise the pile cap," and also failed to work with the supervision unit to review the constructor's earthwork excavation plan and organize expert review. Moreover, during the construction process, Haiqing Company allowed the use of heavy trucks to participate in earthwork excavation and transportation, causing road compaction. Haiqing Company insisted that the project cost was a fixed price and, on the grounds that the constructor's choice of construction method was unrelated to the project owner, failed to heed or respond to the constructor's suggestion to adjust the design plan. Therefore, Haiqing Company should bear corresponding responsibility. As a professional constructor, Zhongxing Company was not prudent enough in bidding for and undertaking the project without seeing the detailed geological investigation report and the reviewed construction drawings. After discovering the special geological conditions, although it made suggestions, it still proceeded with construction recklessly at its own risk after Haiqing Company did not accept them, adopting a laissez-faire attitude towards the quality problems in the pile foundation. This subjective state and practice should receive a negative evaluation. If Zhongxing Company truly cared about project quality, it should have negotiated with Haiqing Company regarding the problems caused by the geological conditions. If negotiation failed, knowing that the project could not continue, it should have taken measures to avoid the expansion of losses. From the start of the construction of the project in question, Zhongxing Company could have taken stop-loss measures by halting construction. However, for its own contractual interests, it acted blindly and, as late as March 6, 2008, even signed a supplementary agreement with Haiqing Company stating: "Considering that Zhongxing Company faces certain construction difficulties and increased earthwork volume, Haiqing Company will provide a one-time subsidy of RMB 420,000 to Zhongxing Company. Haiqing Company will no longer bear any costs for all difficulties and problems encountered by Zhongxing Company during construction, including roads, drainage, collapses, etc., and all such matters shall be borne and resolved by Zhongxing Company itself." Although Zhongxing Company argued that the subsidy in this agreement was only for the increased earthwork volume and not for quality problems, it also indicates that Zhongxing Company overlooked quality risks in pursuit of contractual benefits. Therefore, this Court considers that Zhongxing Company should bear a higher proportion of responsibility for the quality accident than determined in the second-instance judgment.

In summary, the project owner, Haiqing Company, should bear the primary responsibility for the occurrence of the quality problem in the project in question, while the constructor, Zhongxing Company, bears secondary responsibility. This Court finds that the responsibility proportions determined by the second-instance court should be adjusted, with Haiqing Company bearing 70% responsibility for the occurrence of the quality problem in the project in question and Zhongxing Company bearing 30% responsibility.

(2) Whether Zhongxing Company should bear liability for breach of contract.

Haiqing Company, in its application for retrial, claimed that the original contract signed with Zhongxing Company stipulated a construction period from December 20, 2007, to February 22, 2008. Later, due to various reasons raised by Zhongxing Company requesting an extension of the construction period, the parties negotiated and reached a supplementary agreement on February 19, 2008, extending the construction period to March 30, 2008. On March 6, 2008, the parties again agreed in a supplementary agreement that the construction period would still expire on March 30, 2008. Thereafter, the parties did not reach any new consensus on the construction period. Although Zhongxing Company later negotiated with Haiqing Company regarding the foundation pit support scheme and costs, the foundation pit support scheme was work within the scope of Zhongxing Company's contract, and the costs were already included in the fixed lump sum price of the contract. Therefore, the later negotiations could not serve as a reason for Zhongxing Company to extend the construction period. Accordingly, the delay in construction from March 31, 2008, should be attributed to Zhongxing Company, which should bear liability for breach of contract. Zhongxing Company argued in its defense that the construction could not continue and the delay was due to Haiqing Company's reasons, and therefore Haiqing Company should bear responsibility.

This Court holds that, as previously stated, the fundamental cause of the quality problem in the project in question was the relatively special geological conditions of the site. After discovering during contract performance that soil issues affected construction, both parties failed to fulfill their obligations in accordance with the principle of good faith, resulting in construction delays and a quality accident, leading to huge losses in construction costs. Based on the degree of fault of both parties, Haiqing Company should bear the primary responsibility for these losses, and Zhongxing Company bears secondary responsibility.

In addition to the construction cost losses, Haiqing Company also claimed that Zhongxing Company should bear liability for breach of contract due to the failure to complete the project on time. This Court holds that the primary fault for the failure to complete on time due to the quality problem lies with Haiqing Company. Therefore, Haiqing Company's legal basis for claiming liability for breach of contract for the construction period from Zhongxing Company, beyond the construction costs, is insufficient and is not supported by this Court.

(3) How the project payment and suspension losses should be determined.

The construction cost conclusion issued by Yong'an Cost Consulting Company is as follows: the cost of completed works for the foundation project was RMB 11,338,644.49; losses during the suspension period amounted to RMB 2,518,309.41, comprising: labor costs of RMB 880,750, material costs of RMB 1,581,058.77 (engineering entity materials: RMB 1,289,133.17, temporary measures materials: RMB 291,925.60), and machinery costs of RMB 56,500.64. The total amount was RMB 13,856,953.90.

Haiqing Company, in its application for retrial, claimed that the method for appraising the cost of completed works was problematic. It argued that not only should the cost of completed works be appraised, but the cost of the entire project should also be appraised based on the drawings. Then, the ratio of these two costs multiplied by the contract price would yield the cost of Zhongxing Company's completed works calculated according to the contract. This Court holds that since the project was not yet completed and the cost of temporary measures during construction was relatively large, it is difficult to accurately calculate the proportion of completed works to the total project by appraising the construction cost based solely on the construction drawings. Therefore, Haiqing Company's proposed method of using the appraised cost of completed works divided by the cost of works according to the drawings and then multiplied by the fixed price agreed in the contract is not reasonable. The second-instance court's determination on this point was not improper.

Haiqing Company, in its application for retrial, claimed that the material losses of over RMB 1.58 million mentioned in the "Construction Cost Appraisal Report" were not losses and should not form part of the construction cost. The materials, including steel bars, steel plates, construction scaffolding, and some equipment, which Haiqing Company had applied for a court seizure during the first instance, were not incorporated into the project. After the case concluded, Zhongxing Company could take them away, so they should not be part of the construction cost. Moreover, on July 26, 2010, during the enforcement process by the Lianyungang Intermediate People's Court, Zhongxing Company had already taken away all the aforementioned materials on the grounds that they belonged to Zhongxing Company. This Court holds that the material cost of RMB 1,581,058.77 should not be deducted. The reason is: the losses of materials such as steel bars, steel pipes, fasteners, and machinery were caused by Haiqing Company's application for litigation preservation during the first instance. According to Article 96 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, if an application for preservation is erroneous, the applicant shall compensate the person subject to preservation for the losses suffered due to the preservation. Although Zhongxing Company had already taken away these materials during enforcement, which should be offset, and the parties have objections to this, this is a matter for the enforcement procedure and falls outside the scope of trial in this case.

Haiqing Company, in its application for retrial, claimed that the calculation of wages for workers and management personnel was erroneous. First, the appraiser calculated based solely on the wage statements provided unilaterally by Zhongxing Company, without other supporting evidence. Second, the time period and amount of wages determined were highly unreasonable. During the retrial review, Haiqing Company submitted a "Work Contact Sheet" from the supervision unit, arguing that this evidence was sufficient to prove that Zhongxing Company's construction personnel had completely withdrawn from the site by the end of April 2008. Zhongxing Company argued in its defense that the evidence on construction personnel wages had already been cross-examined during the first instance. Given that Haiqing Company did not explicitly require a withdrawal from the site, it was necessary for Zhongxing Company to retain several dozen workers, and it had fulfilled its duty to mitigate losses.

This Court holds that the "Work Contact Sheet" dated April 29, 2008, issued by the Tai'an Taishan Engineering Construction Supervision Consulting Company and submitted by Haiqing Company, was formed before the first-instance litigation. However, Haiqing Company did not submit it during either the first or second instance proceedings. This does not comply with the interpretation of new evidence under Article 44 of the Provisions of the Supreme People's Court on Evidence in Civil Proceedings. Furthermore, regarding the issuer, it was issued by the supervision unit, which has an interest in the project owner, Haiqing Company, and therefore cannot alone serve as the basis for determining the facts of the case. Accordingly, this Court does not admit this evidence. Haiqing Company, in its application for retrial, claimed that the appraiser calculated wages based solely on the wage statements provided unilaterally by Zhongxing Company, without other supporting evidence. This Court holds that although Haiqing Company raised objections, it cannot provide sufficient counter-evidence to overturn it. Moreover, in terms of time and amount, it is not unreasonable. Therefore, this Court finds that the second-instance court's determination regarding the project payment and suspension losses was not improper. Haiqing Company's claim in this retrial request lacks sufficient basis and is not supported by this Court. The completed project payment and suspension period losses for Zhongxing Company amount to RMB 13,856,953.90. Haiqing Company should bear 70% responsibility for these losses, and Zhongxing Company should bear the remaining 30%. Accordingly, Haiqing Company should pay Zhongxing Company RMB 9,699,867.73. Haiqing Company has already paid RMB 7,720,000 in project payments, leaving an outstanding amount of RMB 1,979,867.73. Haiqing Company shall pay this amount to Zhongxing Company, along with interest calculated at the bank loan interest rate for the corresponding period.

In conclusion, this Court holds that some of the grounds for Haiqing Company's retrial application are established. Pursuant to Article 186, Paragraph 1, and Article 153, Paragraph 1, Item (3) of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, the judgment is as follows:

1. Paragraphs 1, 2, and 3 of Civil Judgment No. (2010) Su Min Zhong Zi Di 0012 of the Jiangsu High People's Court are affirmed.
